title: Bubble Sort
intuition: Repeatedly steps through the array, swapping adjacent inverted pairs until the largest elements float to the top.
whyExists: Serves as the canonical introductory sorting algorithm demonstrating pairwise element comparisons and invariant maintenance.
analogy: Air bubbles in water: larger bubbles rise to the surface faster than smaller ones.
coreIdea: In each pass, the pointer j sweeps from 0 to n - i - 1. Whenever a[j] > a[j+1], the two elements are swapped. After pass i, the element at index n - i - 1 is guaranteed to be in its permanent sorted location.

complexity.reason: Performs (n-1) + (n-2) + ... + 1 = n(n-1)/2 comparisons in the worst case in-place.

pitfalls: Iterating to index n instead of n - 1 causing IndexOutOfBoundsException.
Failing to shrink the inner loop bound (n - i - 1), wasting time on already-sorted suffix.
Forgetting to break early if no swaps occurred during an entire pass.
